newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian consumer sentiment rises in Jan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian consumer sentiment rises in Jan.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Wednesday its consumer confidence index rose 4.1 points or 4.0 percent in January.
The rise only partly reversed a 7.4 point drop in December and left the index below its level of last July.

"Given we have had three rounds of official interest rate cuts since the July survey it's disappointing consumer sentiment has not responded more positively," said Bill Evans, Westpac's General Manager, Economics.
Almost all the improvement in optimism came from consumer's perceptions that it was a good time to buy household items.
"Since July there has been no significant increase in any of the family finance or economic expectations components of the index," said Evans.
That suggested the soft labour market was having a key impact on sentiment and offsetting the positive effects of the three rate cuts delivered since the end of July, he said.
"In this enviroment, it is likely the Reserve Bank will move to reduce interest rates again." said Evans.
"However, it will be reluctant to go beyond one more cut giventhe likelihood that the accumulated cuts will eventually have a strong and sharp impact on confidence and spending."
The consumer sentiment index, compiled with the Melbourne Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research, rose to 106.5 from 102.4 in December.
On the question of whether it was a good or bad time to buy major household items the positive differential of those answering 'yes' jumped to 34 in January from 18 in December.
Consumers views on future economic conditions was, on balance, neutral, the Institute said.
They did not believe their household was currently better off financially, but were slightly more confident that their own family fortunes would improve over the next 12 months, it said.
